highlights.title: What to Know About Shamonda Virus Following the First Reported Human Infection
highlights.summary: Although the case is considered exceptional, investigators are working to determine how the infection occurred and whether the pathogen played a role in the patient’s death.
body: France confirmed the death of the first person infected with the Shamonda virus, which is known to affect cattle, sheep, and goats and was previously considered non-transmissible to humans. The French government asserts that, based on current knowledge of this pathogen, there is no risk to the general public. It emphasized, however, that health authorities are continuing to investigate.

The report specifies that the case occurred in Lyon. The patient, who died earlier this month, suffered from severe immunosuppression, making this likely an exceptional case. “The neurological complications observed in the immunocompromised patient prior to his death were most likely related to infection with the Shamonda virus,” the official statement notes.

After animal is bitten by a midge carrying Shamonda virus, the infection has an incubation period of two to three days. Symptoms observed in animals include fever, diarrhea, and a decrease in milk production. When pregnant cows have become infected, the virus can cause miscarriages or severe deformations in the calf.

highlights.title: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
highlights.summary: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it. That’s an important shift. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context…
body: Increasingly, the answer depends on the serving harness—the engineering system surrounding the model, including the architecture, memory management, scheduling, and optimization decisions that determine how efficiently model intelligence becomes a production capability.
For technical executives, that changes where AI investment should go—and what they should demand from the architecture supporting it.
There is no universally “best” model or AI architecture. There is only the right solution for the business problem.

A customer-facing assistant optimized for fast responses has fundamentally different requirements from a document-processing pipeline that can run overnight. An internal knowledge application and a high-volume customer service platform may use the same foundation model but require very different serving architectures.

highlights.title: Bournemouth seal historic win over Amorim's 10-man Milan
highlights.summary: Amine Adli scored a fine free-kick to cap Bournemouth's historic 3-0 win over 10-man AC Milan, which continues their brilliant start to their first-ever European campaign.
body: Ruben Amorim's side are far from the standard of the great Milan teams of the past but this is nonetheless a treasured scalp for Bournemouth who, for the majority of their history, could not have imagined they'd play this fixture. The seven-time European champions, humbled by the Cherries.

It was a wet and wild night on the south coast, with the weather fitting for the chaotic first half, which included Milan captain Mike Maignan being sent off for brutally pushing both hands into Tyler Adams' face at a corner.

That recklessness from the goalkeeper brought Bournemouth their second penalty, which was expertly dispatched by Marcus Tavernier after Justin Kluivert had slotted in the first spot-kick following a Koni De Winter handball.
Another dead-ball moment brought Bournemouth's third. It was a wonderful whip from sub Adli - but Amorim would not have been happy with the Milan wall which broke apart to sum up their sloppiness.

highlights.title: 'Mass Effect Universe' Leak Promised What Fans Have Waited Decades For
highlights.summary: If fans were already sad about BioWare closing down, they're shattered after watching the leaked trailer for Mass Effect Universe. Sure, the trailer was short and a little cheesy — but it could have also signaled a return to form for the stagnant franchise.
body: Because the trailer was leaked, and the game was canceled, we can't judge how well the footage reflected the final vision. Fans were happy to see a familiar face in Liara T'Soni, but they were especially thrilled at the prospect of new buddies. In particular, series devotees were intrigued by the prominent appearance of a male Quarian throughout the trailer. The helmeted alien could well have been the series' first-ever male Quarian star.

So far, the series has only featured a single female Quarian, Tali'Zorah, as a recruitable character. Yet as much as the fandom loves Tali, people were ready to stop arguing over what the nomadic alien should actually look like. Plus, fans have been begging for a male Quarian for ages now, as evidenced by this Reddit post from nine years ago. At the time, some people were skeptical Mass Effect might ever pull it off.

"The population of the Citadel is almost as much as the entire Quarian race," one Mass Effect fan argued. "Considering you have races with populations of tens or possibly hundreds of billions, the Quarians are a footnote in the galactic population."

highlights.title: Supercell hit by cyberattack, but says no player data was affected
highlights.summary: The Clash of Clans developer says it was the target of multiple attacks last week and has notified police and regulators.
body: Supercell has confirmed that an unauthorised party has accessed a platform Supercell used to host company meetings and presentations.

In an announcement on October 21, the Clash of Clans developer said it was targeted by multiple cyberattacks last week, one of which caused the incident. Based on its investigations so far, Supercell believes no player data was affected.

It says it blocked further access, took the service offline and began investigating the platform and its security experts. It has since filed a police report, submitted a notification under the EU Cyber Resilience Act, and notified the Data Protection Ombudsman, but said that because the investigation is ongoing, it cannot share further details at this time.

The videos include current and former employees, as well as some guests and partners who took part in internal events. They may contain people’s names, images and voices, and the names and email addresses of the platform’s users were also accessed.

highlights.title: Raye wins the Mercury Prize with This Music May Contain Hope
highlights.summary: The pop star beat artists like Paul McCartney, Suede and Jade Thirlwall to lift the £25,000 prize.
body: Raye has won the 2026 Mercury Prize for her show-stopping second album This Music May Contain Hope.
A pop record sprinkled with golden age Hollywood glamour, it beat the likes of Sir Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Jade to scoop the £25,000 prize.
"I couldn't tell you how grateful I am to be holding this," said Raye, clutching her trophy at Newcastle's Utilita Arena. "I'm shaking, I'm jet-lagged, I'm tired. It's all blurry."
It is the first time a pop album has won the coveted prize - which recognises the best British or Irish album of the last 12 months - since M People's Elegant Slumming in 1994.

highlights.title: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
highlights.summary: A security researcher has demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Switch 2, gaining "userland" access that he says "lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO." The hack…
body: The hack relies on the original Switch version of SmileBasic 4, the latest in a long-running series of programming environments and interpreters that run on Nintendo hardware. The so-called "tethered" hack also requires access to a macOS or Linux PC on the same network to run a node.js package that helps enable privileged system access.

Researcher Sammy Hajhamid writes that he used OpenAI's Codex to poke at SmileBasic's language interpreter, using a custom harness that could send USB commands to the system and view results via HDMI (as well as power cycling via a Bluetooth light switch flipping device). After "substantial effort for ~2 weeks," that harness discovered a 32-bit integer overflow that occurs when removing items from an array in SmileBasic. That error gives access to an array pointer, which in turn allows read and write access to portions of system memory.

highlights.title: This design software reimagines everyday objects as self-aware devices
highlights.summary: “X-Hinges” helps design and 3D print items like lamps and gloves with an interactive twist: automatically embedded sensors that perceive and adaptively respond to human contact.
body: Jiaji Li and lead author Xiang Chang, a TJU PhD student and visiting researcher at CSAIL, used X-Hinges to create many clever devices. For example, they made a glove that can teach a robot how to grasp blocks. It adjusts to the size of a user’s hands, then records how the joints in their fingers bend via sensors before rapidly relaying that information to a humanoid hand to mimic it. The glove could be useful in factories or homes, where a robot often needs to learn new interactions quickly.

The researchers also produced a small, origami-style lamp using X-Hinges. It senses when a human pinches it closed and adjusts its brightness accordingly. When you turn on this adaptive, portable light source (sort of like a reading light), it looks like a piece of folded-up paper that sprouts into a lamp.

X-Hinges can even assemble devices that identify which objects have been placed on it. You could put a banana on top, for instance, and it’ll recognize the fruit almost immediately based on the tactile data it’s recorded using its sensors. This advanced physical awareness could be integrated into detection systems in places such as airports and grocery stores.

highlights.summary: Jean-Philippe Mateta scored his first goal since last season's UEFA Conference League final but Crystal Palace had to settle for a 2-2 draw away at 10-man Besiktas.
body: Mateta thought he had opened the scoring with the first chance of the match when he swept home in the fifth minute, only for VAR to intervene and rule the striker had strayed marginally offside.
Besiktas took the lead against the run of play when Wilfred Ndidi rifled in on the stroke of half-time with Besiktas' first shot on target.

But Palace equalised six minutes after the restart when Pino got on the end of Anan Khalaili's cutback to sweep in. The flag went up for offside, but this time VAR intervened in Palace's favour with the visitors drawing level.
And four minutes later they went ahead after Mateta intercepted a loose back pass before striding into the area and smashing home into the roof of the net.

highlights.title: Moderna and Merck say their mRNA cancer vaccine cut death, recurrence by 42%
highlights.summary: Personalized mRNA vaccines against melanoma—the deadliest form of skin cancer—reduced the risk of death or recurrence by 42 percent compared to standard treatment in a late-stage trial, pharmaceutical partners Merck and Moderna announced Thursday.
body: The results are a significant advance in melanoma treatment; Merck and Moderna are already engaging with regulatory authorities to get the vaccine approved. More broadly, the vaccine's success bolsters hope that mRNA vaccines and individualized cancer-targeting medicines offer a new paradigm for cancer therapies.

"From the beginning, we believed mRNA technology could make it possible to develop cancer treatments uniquely matched to each patient’s tumor," Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel said in a statement. The trial results "mark a defining moment for that vision and show what’s possible when we rethink how medicines are made." They also "reinforce our conviction that mRNA has the potential to fundamentally change how we treat cancer," he said.

highlights.title: Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
highlights.summary: Meta has tweaked its business terms to remove language suggesting that it could freely train its AI models on news sites, like The Verge - but legal experts say these changes aren't enough to address their concerns.
body: Meta’s new business terms could still help it justify training AI on scraped sites.

Initially, Meta’s new terms for business accounts appeared to give the company permission to train its AI on news sites. The terms, which go into effect October 30th, stated that Meta “may use any content” from the websites associated with a business account to “develop, research” and “train” Meta’s products. At the time, legal experts told Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta “to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions,” such as the robots.txt file that has historically told scrapers (including search engines like Google) what they are allowed to crawl.

highlights.title: How to face the end of the world – according to Plato and the Stoics
highlights.summary: Fearing future catastrophe is nothing new – ancient Greek and Roman philosophers all visualized the apocalypse. Do your feelings of existential dread extend beyond your own personal mortality?
body: Apocalyptic expectations are on the rise. According to a 2022 Pew Research Center survey, 39% of Americans believe that we are living in the end times.

Yet the feeling that the world is coming to an end is nothing new. Anticipating and preparing for the end of the world is an ancient practice. In fact, many of the ways in which we envision future catastrophes can be traced back to the ancient Mediterranean world.

Greek and Roman authors set up their accounts of the end of the world as the product of reason rather than divine revelation – the product of the rational study of the laws of nature that govern the universe. They saw the end of the world as an inevitability and typically saw the aftermath, if there was one, as a repeat of the cycle of human development. The main piece of wisdom they seek to provide is how to face catastrophe without fear.

This is particularly true of the Epicureans and Stoics. Their goal is to meet all events up to and including the end of the world with equanimity. The Roman poet Horace offers a summation of this ideal in his Odes: the “righteous and resolute man” will remain “undaunted even if the sky should fall and the ruins strike his head”.

highlights.title: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.
highlights.summary: NASA does not have, nor want, nuclear weapons. But when it comes to a particular metric that is part of the Artemis Program to land people on the Moon, NASA guards a particular number like they are trying to prevent outsiders from cracking nuclear codes.
body: I am speaking of the number of Starship launches required to fuel a Starship-based lunar lander in low-Earth orbit such that it can fly out to the Moon, land there, and return to lunar orbit.

This number has been a moving target over the years. The general response from NASA has typically been, ‘We don’t know for sure, so we’re not going to say.’ In 2023, for example, the then-director of NASA’s Human Landing System, Lisa Watson-Morgan, told Ars, “We have a general idea, but I’m reluctant to say exactly what that is.”

Later, she said the number was in the “high single digits to the low double digits.” That suggests about a dozen launches, which is a lot. SpaceX would need to launch a “depot” Starship, and then 11 “tanker” Starships to fully load it with liquid oxygen and methane propellant for a lunar voyage. Other officials have said “high teens.” The hope has always been that SpaceX would dramatically improve the lift capacity of Starship to bring down the number of tanker flights.

highlights.summary: Oh sure, SpaceX's credit risk is pretty high because it's about to borrow another $40 billion to spend on Nvidia chips, but who cares about that? SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss a merger!
body: Yes, of course there are pay package incentives in play for Musk. But that’s not all.

The degree to which you find this merger compelling likely has to do with the degree to which you believe Elon Musk about wanting to go to Mars, or “spread the light of consciousness,” as he put it in this week’s SpaceX earnings call (and earlier S-1). Now, a reasonably informed person knows that we don’t have the technology — or, frankly, even the raw information to build the technology — in order to support human life in space. So that means robots. But a lag between Earth and the Moon or Mars makes for difficulty in controlling the robots. So having artificially intelligent robots who can make decisions on their own with minimal supervision from Earth is the next sci-fi logic step.
“There’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software.”

highlights.summary: Annie Potts, who portrayed a younger version of Sheldon’s Meemaw on Young Sheldon, revealed how she felt about the show’s finale, disagreeing with how adult Sheldon remained "mean and unchanged" in Parsons' finale cameo.
body: The end of Young Sheldon — the seven-season-long Big Bang Theory Spinoff show — was rife with drama. Its abrupt ending was reportedly revealed to cast members in a Zoom call, with Potts saying she felt “blindsided” by the decision and went "full Meemaw” on the series’ producers.

She elaborated on these feelings in a book authored by Jessica Radloff titled Young Sheldon: The (Juicier-Than-Meemaw’s-Brisket) Inside Story of the Hit Comedy, where she described her reaction to Jim Parson’s cameo at the end of the final episode as a grown-up Sheldon.
According to Radloff’s book, Potts was “a little sad” about how Sheldon remained “mean and unchanged” as a character despite all the events of the prequel series.

While most of the cast reportedly felt similarly burnt by the situation, Young Sheldon himself, Iain Armitage, said he was probably the only member who was actually happy that the show was finally over.

highlights.title: Half-Life 3 Rumors Reignite After Valve Employee Lets Codename Slip
highlights.summary: It's been two decades since we last checked in on Gordon Freeman in Half-Life 2: Episode Two, with the promise of a third Half-Life game languishing for an absurdly long time.
body: The latest morsel about the long-rumored existence of Half-Life 3 comes after years of leaks about a game codenamed "HLX." One Valve employee just casually dropped the name HLX during a gaming convention this week, restarting the rumor mill.

At this week's GameSoundCon, a game music and sound design conference in Burbank, California, Valve composer Mike Morasky appeared on a panel with sound designers David Feise and Carlye Nyte. Their talk, titled "Valve’s Approach to an Open and Flexible Audio Engine," was meant to discuss Valve's Source 2 audio engine and extensible open systems. What most people will take away from that talk is that Morasky let slip Half-Life 3 's supposed codename HLX in a public forum, seemingly to the chagrin of one of his panelists.

body: Variety wrote of Raye’s album: “Suffice it to say, the album does not lack for ambition: Divided into four sections based on the seasons, it sprawls across a surprisingly fast-moving 70 minutes, 17 songs and nearly as many styles. Inevitably, it runs the risk of being too much for some listeners: too many songs, too many stylistic pivots, too much of… well, basically everything. This is not an album for background listening — it basically demands your attention.

“But as artists from Queen to Beyoncé have proven, ambition and excess can be glorious things when deployed with intelligence and humor, and while we’re not equating Raye with either of the above, there’s a similar sense here of trusting the artist to take you on an interesting voyage without wasting your time.”

highlights.title: Fifi's Wig Shop Brings Halloween Transformations to the Next Level
highlights.summary: Fifi's Wig Shop is a must-stop destinations for elaborate, one-of-a-kind wigs. “In New Orleans, we will always find an excuse to wear a wig.”
body: It makes sense that New Orleans is a hot destination to celebrate Halloween. From the spooky ghost tours to the haunted hotels, the Louisiana city is a prime spot for getting into the macabre spirit. It’s unsurprising, then, that it’s also the best place to find one-of-a-kind costumes, too—and if you so happen to be still in need of an over-the-top wig this Halloween, there’s one particular shop that draws in both locals and tourists alike. Meet Fifi’s Custom Wigs.

The French Quarter wig shop was founded in 1977 by Marcy Hesseling, eventually taken over by Thomas O’Donnell and his husband Neil Ard back in 2023. The couple had just relocated from New York City—where O’Donnell worked in theater, and Ard in fashion—and both saw opportunity as a natural next step for their combined careers.

“I'd taken a part-time job at Fifi's, just for fun,” says O’Donnell. “Then Marcy Willy Wonka-ed us. We bought the business with the intent of carrying the torch for the foreseeable future, and so far, so good!”

highlights.title: Sharp drops for AI stocks overwhelm markets worldwide as oil prices jump
highlights.summary: Datacenter and chip costs fueled sharp decrease in AI sector although non-AI stocks still had a strong showing. The latest shudder for stocks in the AI industry pulled markets lower worldwide on Thursday, while oil prices hit their highest levels since May on worries about the war with Iran.
body: The S&P 500 fell 1.2% for its worst day since July, while the Nasdaq composite tumbled 2.6%. The weakness for tech stocks was so overwhelming that it masked strength for the rest of the US market, in which the majority of stocks actually rose. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 11 points, or less than 0.1%.

AI-related stocks have been swinging on worries that their boom may be under threat because of how expensive it’s become to borrow money to build datacenters and buy more AI chips. Concerns also remain that their prices shot too high following a years-long frenzy, even though companies in the industry continue to report growth.

Lam Research, whose equipment and services help make semiconductors, reported gains in profit and revenue for the summer that were slightly stronger than analysts expected, for example. Usually, that helps boost a stock’s price, but Lam Research’s tumbled 11.8%.
Other big tech stocks likewise fell following quarterly reports that included at least some encouraging nuggets.

highlights.title: Build more responsive apps with the Decisions API
highlights.summary: Fast, focused, low-cost decisions for any application.
body: Applications and agents make many small decisions throughout a workflow: how to classify an input, where to route a request, or which action to take next. Individually, they are simple. At scale, their latency and cost add up.

Today, we’re making the Decisions API generally available. Built with GPT‑6 Luna, the Decisions API focuses Luna’s intelligence on questions with bounded answers, helping applications and agents make near real-time decisions from text, images, and structured inputs up to 10x faster than GPT‑6 Luna through the Responses API.

Since public beta, we’ve added a native GPT‑Live integration, prompt caching for reused context, and inference residency in the US and EU. Developers can also pass native JSON inputs, include images in question instructions, and ask up to 400 questions per request, twice the previous limit. We’ve also continued to improve latency, including additional capacity in several regions in Asia.
Early adoption of Decisions has shown its applicability across a variety of use cases.

highlights.title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix
highlights.summary: 41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’ Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record. Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s.
body: Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.

Hamilton has been championing a race in Africa for some time. The 41-year-old is understood to be currently contracted with Ferrari until the end of the 2027 season, and speaking before this weekend’s US Grand Prix he said he would like to continue racing for at least another four years in order to make it to the meeting in Rwanda.

“I’m now forced to have to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa and that’s been my dream to be able to race in Africa,” he said. “So, I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit if I can. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we’ll keep it going.”
Hamilton would be at least in his mid-40s if he was to continue until 2030. F1’s current oldest driver is 45-year-old Fernando Alonso.
points: 41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’ Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record.

highlights.title: 'Clayface' Officially Sets Up Another Iconic Batman Villain in the DC Universe
highlights.summary: Back in the summer of 2025, Clayface was filming in Liverpool. Photos from the set revealed a reference to another, far more famous Batman villain. One featured a wall with graffiti on it, and among the different tags was one that read “The Jokers.” That led to some speculation about Joker’s…
body: Because “Jokers” is plural, some thought it could be a reference to a DC Comics storyline from 2020, which introduced the idea that instead of one Joker, there are three: the clown, the criminal, and the comedian. That would explain away any personality inconsistencies between varying depictions of the character over 80 years. Others thought “The Jokers” could be a reference to the Joker gang, which is generally portrayed as a gang of street criminals who idolize, and dress like, the Joker. Versions of the gang were featured in Batman Begins as well as The Batman. Some thought it was proof that the Joker himself would appear in Clayface.
Having seen Clayface, I know the answer to these queries, and I can share that there are way more Joker references in this movie.

So, no, the Joker is not in Clayface, much less three of him, nor does the Joker gang appear, but there are a number of references to him. To start off, I’m really not sure if this graffiti even made it into the movie, as it's certainly never focused on, though it may be at the very end of the film, hidden in the background, if anywhere.
